chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:
I said to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: May a woman dye herself with henna while she is menstruating? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, the Imam to whom the legal question was addressed
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.تَخْتَضِبُ: applies dye or henna to herself
key_terms.طَامِثٌ: menstruating; in a state of hayd
key_terms.نَعَمْ: yes; an explicit statement of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a menstruating woman to apply henna or dye?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a concise legal ruling that a menstruating woman may apply dye such as henna. It indicates the permissibility of this act during menstruation and falls under rulings related to hayd and ritual purity.
